subject: Clarify post-pay surcharge allocation and VAT handling for March surge
messages:
From: Marta Gomez <marta.gomez@clearsky.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: finance@clearsky.com
Date: Tue, 27 Mar 2028 09:14:00 -0400
Subject: Unexpected surcharge + VAT on March usage — need allocation detail

Hi Karthik,

We pulled our March invoice and see a ~21% surcharge line labeled "post-pay surge adjustment" plus an EU VAT amount that doesn't match our expectations. This pushed our total ~32% above forecast. Our finance team is asking for:

- A short explanation of what triggered the surcharge and which requests it applies to (per-service breakdown if possible).
- Proof of the usage window / request IDs you used to calculate the surcharge.
- How VAT was applied (which entity and tax basis).

I've attached a one-page usage summary from our side (clearsky_usage_mar2028_summary.csv). Can you confirm whether this is the same dataset you billed against? We need the information to clear this with our AP team before the end of the month.

Thanks,
Marta
Marta Gomez
Head of Cloud Ops, ClearSky Analytics
Attachment: clearsky_usage_mar2028_summary.csv (CSV, 28KB)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Marta Gomez <marta.gomez@clearsky.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Mar 2028 11:02:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected surcharge + VAT on March usage — need allocation detail

Hi Marta — thanks for the heads up and for sending your summary. We dug into the ledger and I want to give you an initial, concrete answer while we pull line-level evidence. High level:

- The "post-pay surge adjustment" is an automated surcharge that kicked in when your daily sustained concurrent tokens exceeded the committed threshold for three consecutive days (Mar 10–12). It is computed on top of the baseline rate per our post-pay terms and is applied to requests in the affected window.
- VAT was applied based on the billing entity tied to your account (Redwood EU Ltd). That made the VAT line appear on the invoice as an EU VAT charge at the local rate for Ireland (23%).

What I'll follow up with by EOD: a CSV export of the request IDs/time ranges we used to compute the surcharge and a reconciliation against the clearsky file you provided.

For now, two quick asks:
1) Can you confirm whether any test traffic from staging (separate API key) was included in the clearsky export? That will speed up matching.
2) Would you like us to hold collections on the surcharge while we reconcile? We can mark the surcharge as "provisional" and remove it from the payment due list temporarily if you need time to validate.

I'll loop in Evelyn (billing) and Ben (account) to coordinate next steps.

Best,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Marta Gomez <marta.gomez@clearsky.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Mar 2028 09:17:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected surcharge + VAT on March usage — need allocation detail

Hi Marta — quick note from the account team. We absolutely want to make this painless. Proposal:

- Evelyn will push the line-level export to you with request IDs and the exact timestamps tied to the surcharge.
- While you validate (48–72 hours), we can mark the surcharge as provisional and exclude it from the payment link.
- If validation shows staging/test traffic caused the spike, we'll issue a retroactive credit and correct the VAT treatment if needed.

If that works, we'll prepare a provisional invoice (attached) showing the surcharge separated out and a "provisional hold" flag. If you need a different cadence, tell us and we'll adapt.

Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: provisional_invoice_DL-9843_20280329.pdf (PDF, 12KB)
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
To: Marta Gomez <marta.gomez@clearsky.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 29 Mar 2028 16:02:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected surcharge + VAT on March usage — need allocation detail

Hi Marta — attached is the line-level export we referenced. Short summary of what you will see in the file:

- Columns: request_id, api_key_hash, timestamp_utc, model, tokens_in, tokens_out, charged_tokens, surge_flag
- Rows with surge_flag=1 are the ones included in the surcharge calculation. The export covers 2028-03-01 through 2028-03-31 and the surcharge window is 2028-03-10T00:00:00Z through 2028-03-12T23:59:59Z.

Next steps for us:
- You validate whether any request_ids map to staging keys (if yes, call that out).
- If you request a provisional hold, we will set the surcharge to "provisional" on the invoice and waive collection until reconciliation completes.
- If validation finds a mismatch in billed entity for VAT (e.g., invoice should have been billed by Redwood US LLC instead of Redwood EU Ltd), we will coordinate a corrected invoice and VAT reversal.

I attached the export to this message and put a copy on the Drive link Karthik shared. Let me know when you start validation and whether you want the hold.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Billing Operations Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachment: usage_export_with_surge_flags_202803.csv (CSV, 1.6MB)
